'''William Alexander Gambling FRS'''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fox |first=Donald |last2=Laming |first2=Richard |date=2025 |title=William Alexander Gambling. 11 October 1926—9 January 2021 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2024.0043 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=78}}</ref> (11 October 1926 – 9 January 2021) was a British electrical engineer known for pioneering work in the field of optoelectronics.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.debretts.co.uk/people/biographies/browse/g/5129/William%20Alexander+GAMBLING.aspx |title=Prof W A Gambling, FRS, FREng Authorised Biography – Debrett's People of Today, Prof W A Gambling, FRS, FREng Profile |website=debretts.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325062637/http://www.debretts.co.uk/people/biographies/browse/g/5129/William%20Alexander+GAMBLING.aspx |archive-date=2012-03-25}}</ref>

==Life==
From 1950 to 1955, he was lecturer in electric power engineering at the [[University of Liverpool]].
He taught at the [[University of Southampton]] and was dean of Engineering and Applied Sciences from 1972 to 1975.

He was president of Institution of Electronic and Radio Engineers in 1978. In 1979, he was elected a [[Fellow]] of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]],<ref>{{cite web|title=List of Fellows|url=http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|access-date=16 October 2014|archive-date=8 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608094405/http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.theiet.org/resources/library/archives/institution-history/presidents-iere.cfm|title = IET Library}}</ref> and Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1983.

He was BT professor of optical communications from 1980 to 1995 and founder and director of the Optoelectronics Research Centre from 1989 to 1995.

He was Royal Society Kan Tong Po visiting professor at the [[University of Hong Kong]] from 1996 to 2001.  He was director of Research and Development at Optoelectronics LTK Industries Ltd from 2002 to 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/g/5129/William+Alexander.aspx |title=Prof W A Gambling, FRS, FREng Authorised Biography – Debrett's People of Today, Prof W A Gambling, FRS, FREng Profile |website=debretts.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911093042/http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/g/5129/William+Alexander.aspx |archive-date=2012-09-11}}</ref>

He was awarded the [[James Alfred Ewing Medal]] in 2002.<ref>The International Who's Who 2004</ref> He died in Spain on 9 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Obituary for Professor Alec Gambling – first Director of Southampton's Optoelectronics Centre |url=https://www.orc.soton.ac.uk/news/6902 |website=Optoelectronics Research Centre, University of Southampton |access-date=31 August 2022}}</ref>

*''Photons and fibres: the new world of communications'', Royal Academy of Engineering, 1992
*S. T. Lee, P. S. Chung, William Alexander Gambling, C. S. Lee, ''Papers presented at the Asia-Pacific Symposium on Organic Electrolumuniscent Materials and Devices'', City University of Hong Kong, 2000
